title: ClawSecure Discloses Critical MCP Protocol Vulnerabilities Affecting Linear, Notion, Dropbox Dash
key_facts: ClawSecure's AI Agent Threat Report says the weakness is in the MCP specification, so it cannot simply be patched
Notion and Linear MCP servers automatically fetch attacker-controlled links when content is created, with no AI involvement
17 of 20 obfuscation techniques survived the round trip
Of 14 models from five labs tested, none consistently blocked the threats; the best, Claude Opus 4.7, obeyed malicious instructions 26.7 percent of the time
Only 8.5 percent of public MCP servers use OAuth
No independent replication, no CVEs and no vendor patches reported
quote_evidence: ClawSecure is a commercial security vendor with a product to sell, and at the time of this reporting, there has been no independent third-party replication of these platform-layer findings.
Furthermore, no specific CVEs or official vendor patches have been issued in response to the report.
why_it_matters_hint: Claimed protocol-level weakness in a standard many AI agents rely on, unconfirmed.
notes: Read in full from the pool link. Forkast stresses ClawSecure is a commercial vendor and nothing has been independently replicated.
